parts.name: spider center

physics.Basic_description: Central cross-shaped metal hub connecting the two yokes, painted light grey.
physics.Functional_description: Transmits torque between the two shafts at varying angles via the four journals.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and internal to grasp directly; manipulation occurs via the yokes.
physics.reason: Forged steel cross component designed to handle high shear loads, typically solid material.

parts.description: Central cross-shaped metal hub connecting the two yokes, painted light grey.

parts.name: shaft yoke

physics.Basic_description: Large U-shaped metal fork with splined shaft, painted light grey, forming one half of the joint.
physics.Functional_description: Connects to one drive shaft and holds one axis of the spider cross.
physics.Grasped_description: Primary grasp target; gripper can clamp onto the splined shaft or the yoke arms.
physics.reason: The splined shaft section is likely a hollow tube to save weight, while the yoke head is thick-walled cast/forged metal.

physics.reason: Thick metal plug designed to withstand internal pressure and retain bearings.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained

simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)
